title: How to Spot GREAT Stocks, Avoid Bad Stocks and Survive Market Cycles - Rahul Jain G2G
creator: Rahul Jain
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; Good to Great collaboration video (collab_byline: Good 2 Great By Rahul Jain and 2 more), guest Ajay Sharma, fund manager and author of 'Good to Great to Gone'; guest states twice that he is not giving recommendations.
summary: Rahul Jain interviews fund manager and author Ajay Sharma about his book 'Good to Great to Gone': every great company stops being great, so investing is as much about knowing when to avoid or exit as when to buy. Sharma's core rule is to avoid the large loss — cap any position at 7% at cost or 10% at market price, and never buy just because a stock has fallen 50-80%. He sorts businesses into Brahma (creation), Vishnu (dominant stability) and Mahesh (decline) phases, and judges industry structure as a lake with fish: profits depend on lake size and fish count. Asian Paints is the case, a 30-year whale at a 70-80 multiple whose dominance broke when Birla Opus entered with Rs 10,000 crore, lifting capacity about 50% against 7% demand growth. HDFC Bank is in an 'exile' of FII selling plus a leadership vacuum: cheap, but it may stay cheap. His sell discipline is a thesis-by-price matrix and an expected-return test — 15% growth for ten years with a multiple decaying from 100 to 25 merely breaks even — so exit when expected return falls below the index plus a premium (5%, about 20% for micro/small caps). Other rules: use median, not average, multiples; investigate promoter selling; and walk away from governance doubts. Companies are case studies only, and Sharma states twice he is not giving recommendations: Adani Ports as a near-monopoly lake, Jio/Airtel as a telecom duopoly, Zomato/Swiggy as a distribution moat, and Anthropic, his February 2024 investment, as luck, not a repeatable process.
